summary: Emerald Isle light at Shag Harbour, Nova Scotia: a Wrayton family light (1877 per NSLPS and Rowlett; 1875 per LighthouseFriends), kept by the Larkins from 1896, discontinued 2004.

access.note: Grounds and tower closed to visitors; the island is privately owned and reached only by boat.

facts.ownership: Lighthouse owned by the Canadian Coast Guard (LighthouseFriends); island privately owned (Rowlett).

events.note: Government-supplied octagonal iron lantern on a wooden tower, $150 (LighthouseFriends; the year is LighthouseFriends' own).
Light began in 1877 (NSLPS; Rowlett gives station established 1877); Wrayton's salary began 7 May 1877 (LighthouseFriends).
Present squat tower, with material from the old tower used for an oil house (LighthouseFriends); Rowlett also gives 1886 for the tower.
5th order 270 degree dioptric apparatus substituted for the catoptric apparatus (Department report, twelve months ended 31 March 1910). NSLPS dates its 5th order dioptric lens to 1922.
Fifth-order dioptric lens showing flashing green, 4 s (NSLPS).

keepers.name: Michael Wrayton
keepers.note: Tended the light unpaid for two years, then paid $100 a year from 7 May 1877 (LighthouseFriends). Drowned about three months after Maria's death (September 1879), with two of his children, when the Ocean Belle went down (LighthouseFriends; the month is not given).

keepers.name: William W. Wrayton
keepers.note: Took charge after his father's death; transferred to Bon Portage in 1881 (LighthouseFriends).

keepers.name: Agnes Wrayton
keepers.note: Known as Aggie; LighthouseFriends says she assisted her brother William, without giving dates. The years are the span of William's keeping.

keepers.name: Arthur M. Wrayton
keepers.note: Drowned in Argyle Bay in 1892, leaving a wife, Alice, and nine children (LighthouseFriends).

keepers.name: Alice Wrayton
keepers.note: Widow of Arthur Wrayton; looked after the light for a couple of years. LighthouseFriends reports a manslaughter charge over a hired hand's death, from which she was later cleared.

keepers.name: J.A. Larkin
keepers.note: Named J.A. Larkin in LighthouseFriends' keeper list. The sources read do not say how he was related to Ephraim Larkin.

keepers.name: Ephraim Larkin
keepers.note: Appointed 18 March 1896 (LighthouseFriends). The 1910 keeper table (page image checked) names him at Stoddart Island but prints the appointment date as Mar. 18, 1806, which does not fit 1896. LighthouseFriends' list says 'at least 1931' while its text says 'over twenty-four years'. Spelled Larken in Saltscapes (2023).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record says sources differ on whether the light is still lit. LighthouseFriends and Rowlett both date the end of the light to 2004 (discontinued early 2004; inactive since 2004). NSLPS's own page calls the light operational and also answers 'No' to still operating, so it is treated as unreliable on this point.
Wikidata's 1877 for the tower is the year the light began (NSLPS, Rowlett). LighthouseFriends and Rowlett date the present tower to 1886.

notes_for_editor: Start date: LighthouseFriends' keeper list begins Michael Wrayton in 1875, and its text dates the government lantern to 1875; NSLPS and Rowlett give 1877 for the light or station. The story states both. Tower: LighthouseFriends and Rowlett give 1886 for the present squat tower; NSLPS gives 21 ft and no date. Lens dates: the Department report (twelve months ended 31 March 1910, printed p. 93, scan 93) records the 5th order 270 degree dioptric apparatus; NSLPS's history starts its 5th order dioptric lens in 1922. The story states the gap. Keeper table (printed p. 258, scan 260): checked on the page image (PDF page 261 of the Internet Archive copy). The row reads Stoddart Island, Ephraim Larkin, Mar. 18, 1806, salary 265.00; the OCR joins it with the Sydney Bar row's June 20, 1872, which belongs to George Nunn. The printed 1806 does not fit LighthouseFriends' 1896, so the table names Larkin at Stoddart but does not confirm the appointment date. Wrayton keepers 1875-1892, the Ocean Belle sinking and Bon Portage material rest on LighthouseFriends alone (copyrighted site: facts paraphrased, one short quotation). No Wrayton appears in the Canadian Marine reports in the corpus (1900-1925 searched). The December 1879 drowning is inferred from LighthouseFriends' 'three months later' after September 1879; the story says 'about three months later'. Agnes Wrayton's years are approximate, taken from her brother's service. Evelyn Fox's birth and marriage come from Saltscapes (2023, copyrighted; facts only), which spells the grandfather 'Larken'. Rowlett's offshore distance (1.1 km) differs from LighthouseFriends (1.6 km); the story gives no distance. Wikipedia used as a lead only.
